assessment.nobel_worthiness: Delineation of GLP-1 as an incretin hormone and its conversion into long-acting agonists that treat type 2 diabetes and obesity is a rare case of basic physiology yielding transformative therapies with very large clinical and societal impact. Originality and clarity are high, and the physiological chain from gut hormone to insulin secretion, appetite and weight is well defined.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across proglucagon/GLP-1 discovery and bioactivity (Mojsov, Habener, Holst, Drucker) and drug development (Knudsen). I propose Drucker, Holst and Mojsov for the physiological and peptide-characterisation core; Knudsen's medicinal chemistry and the role of Joel Habener (not in the supplied names) are unresolved allocation issues.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple independent large outcome trials confirm efficacy in diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular risk; timing is ripe given widespread clinical use.
uncertainties: Fair division between hormone discovery and drug development is contested and the credited list exceeds three people.
Long-term safety and durability of benefits are still being characterised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Channelrhodopsins and their use to control defined neurons with millisecond precision transformed causal circuit analysis. From my perspective as a motor-circuit physiologist, it is a method that opened questions previously intractable, with enormous lasting impact across neuroscience and beyond.
assessment.attribution: Decisive contributions split between microbial-opsin discovery and characterisation (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and demonstration in neurons and tools development (Boyden, Deisseroth, Miesenboeck). Six credited names cannot all be honoured; I propose Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann, acknowledging that Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenboeck have substantial claims.
assessment.maturity: Mature: widely replicated for two decades and deployed in countless laboratories; clinical translation (vision restoration) is emerging but not essential to recognition.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over who first achieved neuronal control make a three-person split contentious.
It is a tool/method award in a field where the Prize has historically favoured discoveries over techniques.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering patient T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and established a new therapeutic modality. The concept is original, the clinical effect striking, and the impact on cancer treatment lasting.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June drove CAR design (costimulation, clinical translation) and Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early clinical gene-modified T cells. The three supplied names support a plausible configuration; the early contributions of Eshhar and others are not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Mature enough: several approved products and many years of follow-up, though toxicity, solid-tumour limits and manufacturing constraints remain.
uncertainties: Omission of early chimeric receptor pioneers from the credited names may complicate fairness.
Long-term durability and secondary malignancy data are still accruing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identifying SMN2 splicing as a correctable lesion and developing the antisense oligonucleotide nusinersen converted a fatal infantile motor neuron disease into a treatable one. This is mechanism-to-therapy at its clearest and is of particular interest to me as a spinal motor-system disease.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and ASO target; Bennett led Ionis's oligonucleotide chemistry and development. Two laureates is a coherent configuration, though the contributions of Adrian Krainer's collaborators and Ionis/Biogen clinical leaders are not itemised.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature: approved since 2016 with long-term clinical follow-up, though recognition may come somewhat earlier than for older candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be seen as recognising antisense technology generally or only SMA is uncertain.
I cannot independently verify detailed priority among splicing-modulation contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of TOR as the target of rapamycin and its role as a central controller of cell growth, nutrient sensing and metabolism is a conceptual advance with consequences for cancer, ageing, immunology and diabetes.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically and defined its biological role; Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin provided the chemical-biological link. Sabatini's mammalian mTOR work is also credited, but I choose Hall and Schreiber while acknowledging that allocation is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Mature: extensively confirmed over three decades, with clinical use of rapalogs in transplantation and oncology.
uncertainties: Attribution among yeast genetics, chemical biology and mammalian mTOR work is contested, and Heitman, Movva and others are not in the credited names.
Clinical benefits of rapalogs beyond transplantation are modest compared with the biology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed an organelle-to-nucleus signalling pathway that reports on protein-folding load, with deep relevance to secretory cell physiology, neurodegeneration and cancer. Originality and clarity are high.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently and jointly delineated the Ire1-Hac1/XBP1 pathway; the two supplied names form a natural pair, with other contributors (e.g. Ron on later branches) not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Mature: pathway steps are well confirmed across species, and modulators are entering the clinic, although therapeutic impact is still developing.
uncertainties: Therapeutic translation is early, so impact is mostly conceptual.
Other UPR branches (PERK, ATF6) and their discoverers are not included.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus and thalamus transformed treatment of advanced Parkinson's disease and tremor, and has provided a model for neuromodulation of motor circuits. Clinical impact is large and enduring.
assessment.attribution: Benabid is the single credited name and clearly central to introducing chronic high-frequency stimulation; however, Mahlon DeLong's pallidal and subthalamic circuit insights and others contributed to target selection and are not supplied, so the prize may be seen as incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Mature: four decades of use in hundreds of thousands of patients with randomised trials confirming benefit.
uncertainties: Mechanism of action of DBS is still debated.
Sole-laureate framing may under-credit basal ganglia circuit work by others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: PCSK9 linked human genetics to a tractable therapeutic target: gain-of-function mutations raise LDL cholesterol while loss-of-function variants lower cardiovascular risk, leading to inhibitory antibodies and siRNA. It is a clean example of human genetic validation leading to a new drug class.
assessment.attribution: Abifadel and Boileau identified gain-of-function mutations, Seidah characterised the proprotein convertase, and Hobbs and Cohen established protective loss-of-function variants and population effects. A three-person limit forces a difficult choice; I propose Hobbs, Cohen and Seidah as spanning genetics and biochemistry while acknowledging Abifadel's priority claim.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: approved inhibitors have outcome-trial evidence of reduced events, though use is still expanding.
uncertainties: Priority between the French discovery of gain-of-function mutations and the later population genetics is sensitive.
Lipid-lowering benefit largely extends the statin paradigm, which may temper perceived novelty.
